subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism Adventure 3: Magnetism and electromagnetic induction
welcome_lead: Today you'll generate EMF with Faraday's law — and feel F=BIL.
meta_desc: Physics — magnetic force F=BIL=qvB, Faraday's law ε=-dΦ/dt, Lenz's law.
final_note: You learned current in B field feels F=BIL; charge q at v⊥B feels F=qvB; changing flux induces EMF (Faraday); Lenz: induced opposes change.

concepts.def: Flow of charge and the energy per unit charge driving it.
Opposition to current flow; V = IR.
Region where a magnetic material or current feels a force.
A current-carrying coil that acts as a magnet.
A current-carrying wire in a magnetic field experiences a force.
A changing magnetic field induces a potential difference.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Current-carrying wire in B field:

F = B I L sinθ

F in N, B in T, I in A, L in m.

Direction by Fleming's left-hand rule.
Application: electric motor.

Moving charge in B field:

F = q v B sinθ

Always perpendicular to v → causes circular motion:

r = mv/(qB).

Cyclotrons, mass spectrometers, particle accelerators.

Magnetic flux: Φ = BA cosθ (Wb).

Changing Φ induces EMF: ε = -dΦ/dt (Faraday).

Negative sign = Lenz's law: induced current creates a B that opposes the change.

Application: generator, transformer (mutual induction), induction cooktop (eddy currents).

options: Intensity has no effect on anything in the photoelectric effect.
